This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from the respondents, for the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 15-04-2024, the petitioner was going towards Bengaluru City from her village Rayappanahalli, as a pillion rider, on a motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-03-ES-6444,
ridden by her relative Mahesh P., along with another pillion rider, slowly, cautiously,
on the correct side of Shidlagatta- Bengaluru road.

On the way at about 8.40 a.m.,
infront of Primary School, Ramalingapura Village, Shidlagatta Taluk,
Chikkaballapura District, the driver of the car bearing Reg. No.KA-40-A-9477 came from Shidlagatta side, with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, came towards wrong side of the road and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, all the occupants of the motorcycle knocked down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital, Chikkaballapura, wherein she took first aid treatment and then she was shifted to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, she was a student, studying in 4th standard.
But, due to the accidental injuries, she has lost one academic year of studies.
The Dibburahalli Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.
4. The respondent No.1 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

He has contended that, the driver of his car bearing No.KA-40-A- 9477 was driving the same on the Madhushree M vs Srikanth H N on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105796803/
2 left side of Shidlaghatta road, slowly, carefully and cautiously, by observing all traffic rules and regulations, as there was no traffic on the said road.

5. Whereas, the respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of car bearing Reg.
No.KA-40-A-9477 in favour of respondent No.1 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It seeks protection under Section 56, 66, 147, 149(2) and 150 of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non- compliance of provision under Section 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it is contended that, the car bearing No.KA-40-A-9477 was not at all involved in the alleged accident, the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA- 03-ES-6444 was solely responsible for the alleged accident, the said car is falsely implicated by the petitioner in collusion with the owner of the vehicle, hospital authorities and police, to get compensation from this respondent.
Further it is contended that, the petitioner was not wearing helmet as on the date of accident.
As such, he has violated Section 129 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it is contended that, as per the police documents, three persons were traveling on a two-wheeler, in the event of three persons traveling on a motorcycle each one of them has contributed their negligence in causing the accident.
Further it is contended that, the driver of the car was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the particular class of vehicle as on the date of accident.
The respondent No.1 knowing fully well that the driver did not have valid driving licence as on the date of accident has entrusted his vehicle to the said driver.
The jurisdictional police after investigation filed charge-sheet against the insured vehicle driver under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C. and 181 of Motor Vehicles Act.
Thereby, the owner of the vehicle has committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
Further it is contended that, the car bearing No.KA-40-A-9477 was not holding valid fitness certificate and permit as on the date of accident.

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?

12. On meticulously going through the above police documents marked as Ex.P.3, 8 to 12,
prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-40-A-9477 and dashing the same to the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-03-ES-6444 of the petitioner, from opposite direction.
Due to said impact the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous on her right leg.

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.12, has clearly stated that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg.
No.KA-40-A-9477.
13.

At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of car bearing Reg. No.KA-40-A-9477 in the said accident, issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of said vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

But, the respondent No.1 & 2 have specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has taken place solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-03-ES-6444 and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of car bearing Reg.

Further it is contended that, the petitioner in collusion with the police authorities and respondent No.1 has got registered a false case against the driver of said car, to get wrongful gain from the respondents.
But, the respondents have failed to establish the said contentions.

They have neither adduced any evidence, nor they have produced any document to show that, the said accident has taken place solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-03-ES-6444 himself and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-40-A-9477.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg.
No.KA-40-A-9477 and dashing the same to the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-03-ES-6444 of the petitioner, from opposite direction

. Though, the learned counsel for respondents No.1 and 2 have cross- examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-03-ES-6444 or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

sentences.text: But, it is pertinent to note that, admittedly, at the time of accident the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-ES- 6444 was riding the same along with two pillion riders.

There are every chances that, due to three persons traveling on a motorcycle, which is meant for two persons, there would be congestion to the rider of said motorcycle and he might have lost control resulting in the accident.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-ES-6444 is also liable for contributory negligence in the cause of accident.

But, as there is no evidence on record to show that, the very act of three persons riding on the motorcycle has directly contributed either to the accident or to the impact of the accident upon the victim, this Court is of the opinion that, holding the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-ES- 6444 liable for contributory negligence to the extent of 10% would be justified and will meet the ends of justice.

15. Further, the Ex.P.10 spot mahazar and Ex.P.11 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on left side of Dibburahalli-Shidlagatta road, infront of Primary School,
Ramalingapura Village, Shidlagatta Taluk, Chikkaballapura, in between car bearing Reg.
No.KA-40-A- 9477 and oncoming motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-ES-6444 of the petitioner.
It is not the case of the respondents that, the accident has taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA- 40-A-9477.

Further, the investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.12, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-40-A-9477.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the owner-cum-driver of offending vehicle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

16. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.3 wound certificate, Ex.P.4 discharge summary,
Ex.P.5 OPD book, Ex.P.7 x-rays (total 4), Ex.P.13 discharge summary, Ex.P.15 disability assessment chart, Ex.P.16 x-rays (total 2) and Ex.P.19 case sheets (total 2) it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in the road traffic accident.
The petitioner has sustained fracture shaft of right femur.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondents No.1 and 2 to show that, the above medical records are false documents.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents No.1 and 2 have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg.
No.KA-40-A-9477 and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the said accident.
17.
Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) 11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal Madhushree M vs Srikanth H N on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105796803/

Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, she has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 15-04-2024 at about 8.40 a.m., on Dibburahalli-Shidlagatta road, in front of Primary School, Ramalingapura Village,
Shidlagatta Taluk, Chikkaballapura, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-40-A-9477.
But, the petitioner has failed to prove that, the said accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.

For the reasons stated supra this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner/rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-ES-6444 is also liable for contributory negligence to the extent of 10% in the cause of accident.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Partly Affirmative.
20. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the accident in question has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg.
No.KA-40-A-9477 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, she has sustained fracture shaft of right femur and for the said injury she has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.
To prove her age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of her Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.2.
As per Ex.P.2, the date of birth of the petitioner is 05-11-2015.
The accident has taken place on 15-04-2024 at about 8.40 A.M.
This clearly goes to show that, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 9 years.
In the case in hand, petitioner is admittedly a minor of the age of 9 years as on the date of accident and she has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment,
attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages,
such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.
21.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Master Mallikarjun V/s Divisional Manager, National Insurance Co. Ltd., and another, reported in (2014) 14 SCC 396, has clearly held that, "Though it is difficult to have an accurate assessment of the compensation in the case of children suffering disability on account of a motor vehicle accident, having regard to the relevant factors, precedents and the approach of various High Courts, we are of the view that the appropriate compensation on all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant, etc. should be, if the disability is above 10% and up to 30% to the whole body, Rs.3 lakhs; up to 60%, Rs.4 lakhs; up to 90%, Rs.5 lakhs and above 90%, it should be Rs.6 lakhs.

22. As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the above cited decision, the petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
i) Pain and suffering already undergone and to be suffered in future, mental and physical shock, hardship, inconvenience, and discomforts, etc. and loss of amenities in life on account of permanent disability:
The petitioner has averred that due to accidental injuries, she has sustained grievous injuries and suffered physical disability.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor, who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has sustained fracture shaft of right femur and for the said injury she has undergone surgery i.e. ORIF with TENS nailing under GA.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability of 36.99% to the right lower limb and 12.33% to the whole body.
The Ex.P.3 wound certificate, Ex.P.4 discharge summary, Ex.P.5 OPD book, Ex.P.7 x-rays (total 4),
Ex.P.13 discharge summary, Ex.P.15 disability assessment chart, Ex.P.16 x-rays (total 2) and Ex.P.19 case sheets (total 2)
are clear evident that, the petitioner has suffered the above mentioned injury and she has undergone surgery for the said injury.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions that, the petitioner has not suffered any disability and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that,
the accident has occurred on 15-04-2024 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 04-10-2025, which is after lapse of one year and five months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.2 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, the fractures are united, implants are removed and the petitioner is of tender age of about 10 years.

Therefore,
considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that,
considering the disability of 11% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 11% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
As per the ratio laid down in the above decision, since the disability to the whole body of the petitioner is 11%, she is entitled to compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- under this head.
ii) Discomfort, inconvenience and loss of earnings to the parents during the period of hospitalization:

In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injury i.e.,
fracture shaft of right femur and for the said injury the petitioner has undergone surgery i.e. ORIF with TENS nailing under GA.

8 summaries (total 2), the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 10 days in Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru.

iii) Medical and incidental expenses during the period of hospitalization:

Taking into consideration the distance in between the above places, compensation of Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.

In such circumstances, question of awarding compensation to the petitioner towards future medical expenses does not arise.
Hence, no compensation is awarded under the head future medical expenses.

24. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-40-A- 9477.
The insurance policy issued by the respondent No.2 bearing No.13522742, in respect of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-40-A-9477, was valid from 12-06-2023 to 11-06- 2024.
As such, the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.2 in respect of offending vehicle was valid as on the date of accident.
Further, there is no evidence on record to show that, there is breach of any terms and conditions of the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.2.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-40-A-9477 the accident in question has taken place.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons,

opennyai_summary.arguments:
The respondent No.1 knowing fully well that the driver did not have valid driving licence as on the date of accident has entrusted his vehicle to the said driver.
The jurisdictional police after investigation filed charge-sheet against the insured vehicle driver under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C. and 181 of Motor Vehicles Act.

opennyai_summary.issue:

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?

Shidlagatta Taluk, Chikkaballapura, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-40-A-9477.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
There are every chances that, due to three persons traveling on a motorcycle, which is meant for two persons, there would be congestion to the rider of said motorcycle and he might have lost control resulting in the accident.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-ES-6444 is also liable for contributory negligence in the cause of accident.
But, as there is no evidence on record to show that, the very act of three persons riding on the motorcycle has directly contributed either to the accident or to the impact of the accident upon the victim, this Court is of the opinion that, holding the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-ES- 6444 liable for contributory negligence to the extent of 10% would be justified and will meet the ends of justice.
When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA- 40-A-9477.
Further, the investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.12, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-40-A-9477.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents No.1 and 2 have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg.
No.KA-40-A-9477 and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the said accident.
17.
Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
18. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
Therefore,
considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that,
considering the disability of 11% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 11% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
ii) Discomfort, inconvenience and loss of earnings to the parents during the period of hospitalization:
In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injury i.e.,
fracture shaft of right femur and for the said injury the petitioner has undergone surgery i.e. ORIF with TENS nailing under GA.
Further, there is no evidence on record to show that, the petitioner is in need of any further treatment for the injuries suffered in the accident.
In such circumstances, question of awarding compensation to the petitioner towards future medical expenses does not arise.
Hence, no compensation is awarded under the head future medical expenses.
As such, the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.2 in respect of offending vehicle was valid as on the date of accident.
Further, there is no evidence on record to show that, there is breach of any terms and conditions of the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.2.
Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-40-A-9477 the accident in question has taken place.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
